label: slave-basket-verify
_why: FINDINGS F27 models slave consumption as a BUILDING purchase (SLAVE_BASKET_* defines) whose size is set by how many slaves work non-subsistence buildings; slaves in subsistence get SLAVE_BASKET_SUBSISTENCE_GOODS_MULT = 0.05 of the basket. The derivation was calibrated against DIRECTLY MEASURED 'purchased for slaves' figures for the AMERICAN market only (session 20260802_233029 runs 007/008), where it lands at 0.209 against a measured 0.225. Its boldest untested claim is BRITAIN: none of the market's 10.5M slaves (rural India) reach a real building, so the channel collapses to the 0.05 floor - supported so far only by the weaker residual test. This batch measures the British market directly.
_note: ONE market per run, per the 20260802_233029 note: Goods.GetMarketBuyOrdersBreakdown returns multi-KB formatted tooltip text per good and two markets in one run overflowed the 5x512KB log ring. Even one market usually loses its tail, and each run truncates at a DIFFERENT good, so each market runs several times and the goods are unioned. GBR gets 4 runs because it is the unmeasured case and its good coverage matters most; USA gets 2 more to extend the 34-of-72-good coverage the existing session gave (notably oil, glass and wine, which the model predicts but no run has yet captured). Arm is config/mod_config.json unchanged, i.e. the same build as the session the American numbers came from, so old and new runs are comparable. PARSING: the line renders as '<value>! purchased for ' + a format-control byte + 'slaves! Slaves' - grep 'purchased for', never the full phrase, or it silently returns nothing.
